summary:
FarmShift is a web-based decision-support prototype that helps farmers and field officers compare crop-rotation options under changing weather and farm conditions. The pilot focuses on Majalengka, West Java, and uses 210 days of historical NASA POWER weather data from 2024. It estimates crop water demand using the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith method, then compares nine two-season rotation paths involving rice, maize, and soybean. Users can explore how water access, soil conditions, and farming priorities affect each option, and review clear explanations of the results. FarmShift does not predict yields or prescribe one “best” crop. It helps users understand risks and trade-offs before making a decision.

details:
FarmShift turns weather data and farm information into an interactive comparison of crop-rotation choices. In the Majalengka pilot, users can set basic farm conditions such as soil type, drainage, irrigation access, and farming priorities. The system compares nine two-season paths using rice, maize, and soybean.

It uses 210 days of NASA POWER daily weather data (1 June–27 December 2024). The FAO-56 Penman–Monteith method is used to estimate reference evapotranspiration and crop water demand. Users can compare the NASA-based baseline with clearly marked synthetic drier scenarios, see which options face water limits, and open a “Why?” panel that explains the data, calculations, assumptions, and limits behind each result.

FarmShift is designed for smallholder farmers and field officers. It was built with Python, Pandas, NumPy, Requests, Matplotlib, and Streamlit. The web views use HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Leaflet, and Chart.js. The interface is available in English and Indonesian and includes an interactive map and printable field plans. FarmShift supports planning; it does not forecast yields or automatically tell farmers what to plant.
